lead_story.topic: Bob Pettit, NBA's first MVP and Hall of Famer, dies at 93
lead_story.headline: Bob Pettit, NBA's first MVP, dies at 93
lead_story.research_notes: Bob Pettit won the NBA's first-ever MVP award in 1956 and became the first player in league history to eclipse 20,000 career points. Two-time NBA champion with the Hawks (1958 St. Louis, won again in 1960). 11-time All-Star, four-time All-NBA First Team. Household-name bar: Pettit does NOT clear the test (your non-sports-fan parent would not recognize him unprompted). This is NOT a massive story override — it is a respectful supporting story, not a lead over active playoff-clinching games and a primetime NFL blowout. The lead today is the Falcons-Packers game (Tier 1 calendar: NFL regular season Thursday night, plus Michael Penix's return story). Pettit gets full obituary treatment as a strong supporting story. Research: rank Pettit among first-generation NBA stars (pre-Russell Celtics dynasty). How does his scoring milestone compare to Mikan, Cousy? What was the NBA like in 1956 when he won that first MVP — how many teams, what was the league's footprint? Pettit's Hawks won championships in a league that looked nothing like today's NBA. His 20,000-point milestone came in an era when the game was far less prolific offensively. Give the reader that context — the achievement's scale in its time, not just the raw number.
lead_story.gif_concept: Grief and respect for a foundational figure in NBA history whose name has faded from casual memory but whose achievements were monumental in their era

beats.angle: Pettit's death at 93, his place as the NBA's first MVP and first 20,000-point scorer
beats.landing: Grief and respect for a foundational figure in NBA history whose name has faded from casual memory but whose achievements were monumental in their era

supporting_stories.topic: Guardians clinch playoff berth, could break MLB's longest World Series drought
supporting_stories.headline: Guardians clinch, eye longest drought

tweets.text: The Cleveland Guardians are back in the postseason!

supporting_stories.research_notes: Cleveland clinched playoff berth with 1-0 shutout of Red Sox per ground truth/CBS Sports/TalkinBaseball. Angel Martinez solo HR only run per TalkinBaseball. CBS Sports: Guardians could break MLB's longest World Series drought (last won 1948 — 78 years). Three reasons why: weak American League, strong pitching staff, could be October surprise. Research: rank MLB's active WS droughts. How does 78 years compare to Cubs' 108-year drought (ended 2016), Red Sox 86 years (ended 2004)? Guardians have been close: lost WS 2016 (3-1 lead blown vs Cubs), lost WS 1997 (blown save Game 7 vs Marlins), lost 1995 (vs Braves). The city's sports curse: Browns haven't won since 1964, Cavs finally won 2016. If Guardians win it all, it ends the second-longest active drought in MLB (only Mariners, who've never won, would be longer). That context IS the story — the weight of history, not just this season's playoff berth.

beats.angle: Guardians clinch playoff berth with 1-0 shutout, Martinez solo shot the only run
beats.landing: Respect for a team that does it with pitching and defense in a launch-angle era

beats.angle: The 78-year World Series drought and how it ranks among MLB's longest
beats.landing: Awareness of the historical weight — this isn't just a playoff berth, it's a chance to end generational suffering

supporting_stories.topic: Brewers clinch No. 1 overall seed, reach 100 wins for first time in franchise history
supporting_stories.headline: Brewers clinch No. 1 seed, 100 wins

tweets.text: The Milwaukee Brewers have clinched MLB's No. 1 overall seed in the playoffs

supporting_stories.research_notes: Milwaukee clinched MLB's No. 1 overall seed per TalkinBaseball — first 100-win season in franchise history per TalkinBaseball/StatMuse. Jake Bauers 8th-inning go-ahead hit vs Phillies per TalkinBaseball. Beat Philadelphia 5-1 per ground truth. Research: Brewers franchise started 1969 as Seattle Pilots, moved to Milwaukee 1970. In 57 seasons, never won 100 games until tonight. Previous high: 96 wins in 2011, 2018, 2021. How rare is a first-time 100-win season for a team this old? Compare to other expansion-era franchises — Royals did it 1977 (year 9), Blue Jays 1985 (year 9), Mets 1969 (year 8). Brewers took 57 years. Best season in franchise history, and it's not close. Home-field advantage throughout playoffs. Gary Sanchez's LeBron wristband per JomboyMedia. Team's ceiling is higher than it's ever been.

beats.angle: First 100-win season in 57-year franchise history, No. 1 seed locked
beats.landing: Joy and disbelief — the Brewers have never been this good, and the moment finally arrived
